purpose: The ordered ratification worklist: every live/readiness.json pending-ratification type, batched by service family in COVERAGE.md's usage-weighted order, with each type's evidence pointer. Produces no admission itself - see this file's package doc comment for the family rule and tools/row-gen/propose.go for the PROPOSE evidence channel.

inputs.propose_summary: row-gen -propose: 20 rule class(es) considered (min sample 5), 5 qualify at 100% historical adoption, 1 new logical type(s) proposed for auto-admission

batch_template.note: Issue #426's 'Batch template' section, instantiated once per batch when a follow-up unit files the per-batch issues: SERVICE-FAMILY is the batch's family field, N is len(types).
body_spot_check_steps: Open the provider documentation's Import section (or Identity Schema block, where the evidence pointer says the entry came from precedence evidence) for the type and confirm the pasted argument or attribute is what that section documents.

Confirm the type creates or exports no credential material. If it does, do not paste it - record the rejection by name in tools/row-gen/rejected.json with a reason, so PROPOSE and future batches never offer it again.
Paste the printed block(s) unedited into tools/row-gen/ratified.json, then re-run `go run ./tools/row-gen -emit`.
Build the cohort estate, run the suites, and get a floci probe before merging - the same as any hand-ratified batch.
accept: Types admitted with fixtures and tests.
Golden diff (internal/live/check's TestIdentityGolden) explained line by line.
live/readiness.json regenerated and docs re-rendered in the same PR.
Per-type evidence listed in the PR description.

evidence.rejected_reason: identity verifies cleanly (server-assigned via id, confirmed against the provider's Import section) but internal/live/discovery/tagging_test.go's TestJoinTaggedResourceRealArtifacts and TestTaggableSetCoversAdmissionTable-adjacent fixtures name this exact type, by constant (unswept = "aws_ec2_carrier_gateway"), as the canonical 'mapped in live/mapping.json but not in identity.DefaultTable' real-artifact example (residue.go's own comment traces the aws_instance -> aws_nat_gateway -> aws_ec2_carrier_gateway baton this fork has passed before; a prior batch tried swapping the fixture to aws_verifiedaccess_group and reverted when that swap needed a live/mapping.json via this package's Roster does not count as mapped). Admitting this type breaks that fixture. Left unadmitted; the fix is swapping the fixture's canonical example in internal/live/discovery, outside this batch's write surface.

issue #245's composite-bucket ratification batch: the provider's own Import section documents TWO distinct forms - `account_id:name` for an access point on a general-purpose S3 bucket, and a bare ARN (`arn:aws:s3-outposts:...:accesspoint/NAME`) for one on an S3 on Outposts bucket, chosen by which kind of bucket the access point belongs to, not by which of the two arguments is present. identity.Component's OmitIfAbsent only expresses an optional SEGMENT within one fixed grammar (aws_lambda_permission's qualifier is the precedent); it cannot express two entirely different ID grammars for the same type. A fuller extraction would need a discriminated-union identity shape - an ARN-template form (the 'proposed: assembled template' bucket's own mechanism) alongside the composite form, chosen by whether `bucket` resolves to an Outposts ARN - which does not exist yet.

the classifier's client-named proposal captured only account_id, but the provider's Import section requires account_id AND the Multi-Region Access Point's name, colon-separated - account_id alone does not distinguish between multiple MRAPs in the same account. Left unadmitted.

the classifier's client-named proposal captured only table_bucket_arn, but the provider's Import section requires table_bucket_arn, namespace and name, semicolon-separated - table_bucket_arn alone does not distinguish between multiple tables in the same bucket. Left unadmitted.

issue #427's hand-separator evidence sweep (2026-08-29): the provider's Import section names the separator and both segments in plain prose - "using the `cluster_name` and `identity_provider_config_name` separated by a colon (`:`)" - worked example `example-cluster:example-config` (`terraform import aws_eks_identity_provider_config.example example-cluster:example-config`; the page also documents the 1.12+ identity-block form with the same two named fields). row-gen's own scraped row resolves separator=':' and composed_of_arguments=true but captures only cluster_name as a matched argument, because identity_provider_config_name - though a plain Required field per the doc's own prose - is Required *inside* the resource's required, max_items:1 `oidc` nested block, not a top-level Argument Reference entry; the classifier's top-level-only match cannot cross that boundary without a Block-aware component (the same gap this repo's aws_autoscaling_traffic_source_attachment admission used a Component.Block field, issue #310, to close). Registry: primary_identifier=["IdentityProviderConfigName", "ClusterName", "Type"] names a third segment, Type, that the documented import ID does not carry at all - Type is a create_only argument alongside Oidc and ClusterName, and every example in the doc is the OIDC identity provider (the only kind IAM currently returns for this resource), so the omission looks like a fixed "oidc" literal rather than a real third component; a ratifier should confirm that reading against the provider's own Go source rather than infer it from the CFN registry alone. Unlike this ledger's other apigatewayv2/api_gateway/identitystore/lexv2models entries in this batch, this type is taggable (live/survey-full.json signals.taggable=true at v6.59.0, path 'marker') and so is NOT part of the untaggable, BLOCKED-ON-#233 population those entries name - the ordinary Components-based ratification path applies once a Block-capable component is available.

identity verifies cleanly (server-assigned via id, confirmed against the provider's Import section) but live/residue.go's DeprecatedServices roster hand-excludes the entire aws_pinpoint_ prefix: AWS announced Pinpoint end-of-support for October 30, 2026, folding existing functionality into End User Messaging, and internal/live/lint/residue_test.go's TestRefusalNamesDeprecatedServiceCohort names this exact type, by construct, as the cohort's own fixture. Admitting it breaks that fixture and contradicts the maintainer's own deprecated-service policy, which is not an identity-correctness question this batch's evidence can override. Left unadmitted.

CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (#242, wall/servermint): the sentence above is accurate about the import ID's shape and wrong about what that shape costs. A composite whose parent scope is config-supplied and whose remaining segment is server-minted is not outside this table's vocabulary - internal/live/identity/table_generated.go carries 51 ServerAssigned rows with a separator in their ImportSyntax, and ImportSyntax is documentation only (TypeIdentity's own doc comment): a ServerAssigned row never builds its identity from Components, it reads it back from discovery. The actual blocker is SERVER-ASSIGNED IDENTITY WITH NO MARKER-CAPABLE ARGUMENT, BLOCKED ON #233. live/survey-full.json records signals.taggable=false for this type at v6.59.0, so admitting it would put every instance in NeedsDiscovery, make stamp.go:743's mustStamp true, and raise an unconditional unstampable fatal at stamp.go:537 - and live-mv's locateByList (mv.go:673) would match on a tofu-address tag that cannot exist, reporting "No live resource carries estate X and address Y" about an account it never checked. That is strictly worse than today's refusal, which is why this stays. EVIDENCE FOR THE SHAPE, recomputed from committed artifacts rather than quoted: live/import-grammar.json's own per-segment attribution for this type labels "the action group ID" from the doc's Attribute Reference and "the agent ID", "the agent version" from its Argument Reference. The four taggable members of the same bucket (aws_ecs_task_set, aws_eks_pod_identity_association, aws_prometheus_anomaly_detector, aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace) were admitted in the same batch, because for them the ownership marker is the discriminator and the parent scope only narrows the candidate set: parent-scoped enumeration can CONFIRM an identity the configuration has already narrowed to one, it cannot SUPPLY one.

the pinned provider's import leaves multiplex_id (ForceNew) unset - reproduced directly against floci 2026-08-14: terraform import by the documented PROGRAM_NAME/MULTIPLEX_ID id populates program_name and settings but not multiplex_id, so a marker-rebuilt plan always proposes replacement (#124). identity verifies cleanly (client-named via name, confirmed against the provider's own Identity Schema, v6.59.0 Required: name) but live/residue.go's hand-curated emulatorBlocked roster excludes it outright: "floci answers ssm:CreateDocument with UnsupportedOperation, so no SSM document can be created against the emulator at all (choudoufu#26)", and internal/live/lint/residue_test.go's TestRefusalNamesEmulatorBlockedCohort names this exact type, by construct, as the cohort's own fixture. Admitting it breaks that fixture and outruns what this batch's e2e/floci validation can confirm. Left unadmitted.

verifies cleanly (server-assigned via ARN) but ties with the already-admitted aws_iam_policy under internal/live/identity/parent.go's _policy suffix convention: both are fourteen characters, and lexicographically 'aws_fms_policy' < 'aws_iam_policy', so parentByConvention's shortest-then-alphabetical tie-break risks silently redirecting a policy_arn-shaped argument's convention match away from aws_iam_policy once aws_fms_policy joins DefaultTable (live/e2e/estates/remainder/README.md, 'A naming collision the identity package's convention-based parent inference cannot disambiguate'). Left unadmitted; the fix belongs in parent.go's tie-break rule, out of this batch's write surface.

the registry's primaryIdentifier (ApplicationId alone) undersells the real identity: the provider's Import section requires APPLICATION-ID,DEPLOYMENT-ID (a deployment is one of potentially many under an application), so the classifier's client-named proposal (application_id alone) would resolve every deployment under one application to the same identity - a genuine wrong-object risk. Left unadmitted.
